extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, editors, and staff of medical journals
extracted.subtask_description: The ICMJE 'Recommendations' are formal, cross-journal guidance for the conduct, reporting, editing, and publication of scholarly work in medical journals, covering authorship, disclosure, editorial responsibilities, publication ethics, manuscript preparation, clinical trials, and AI use. This page is the web Table of Contents for the full Recommendations (updated January 2026) with a downloadable PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: A. Purpose of the Recommendations (section I.A) — describes the goals and intended outcomes of the Recommendations for conduct, reporting, editing, and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page shows the TOC only; the full text in the downloadable PDF or individual section pages contains the detailed purpose statement and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Should Use the Recommendations?
rubrics_metrics.description: B. Who Should Use the Recommendations? (section I.B) — identifies the individuals and organizations for whom the Recommendations are intended (e.g., authors, editors, reviewers, journals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TOC entry; consult the full Recommendations for explicit audience guidance and examples of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: History of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: C. History of the Recommendations (section I.C) — outlines the development and revision history of the ICMJE guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TOC entry; historical context and prior versions are available in full text and archived announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining the Role of Authors and Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: II.A Defining the Role of Authors and Contributors — criteria and guidance for who qualifies as an author, contributor roles, and responsibilities (authorship standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full guidance (authorship criteria, contributor lists, acknowledgments, and disputes) is in the main Recommendations text and PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Financial and Non-Financial Relationships and Activities, and Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: II.B Disclosure of Financial and Non-Financial Relationships and Activities, and Conflicts of Interest — standards requiring disclosure of relevant financial and non-financial relationships and potential conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed disclosure requirements and examples are provided in the Recommendations and associated disclosure forms (linkable from the site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities in the Submission and Peer-Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: II.C Responsibilities in the Submission and Peer-Review Process — expectations and duties for authors, reviewers, and editors during submission and peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on confidentiality, timeliness, reviewer conduct, handling of manuscripts, and related responsibilities in the full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Owners and Editorial Freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: II.D Journal Owners and Editorial Freedom — guidance on maintaining editorial independence from owners, sponsors, and advertisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Recommendations discuss safeguards, policies, and examples supporting editorial freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Research Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: II.E Protection of Research Participants — standards for protecting human subjects and other research participants, including ethical oversight and consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed requirements (e.g., IRB/ethics committee approval, informed consent, vulnerable populations) are in the full document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and Version Control
rubrics_metrics.description: III.A Corrections and Version Control — policies for issuing corrections, retractions, errata, and managing versions of published work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Recommendations provide procedures, criteria for corrections vs retractions, and version-tracking best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: III.B Scientific Misconduct — definitions and policies for handling allegations of fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, and other misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full text contains investigative procedures, reporting responsibilities, and recommended actions for journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: III.C Copyright — guidance on copyright ownership, licensing, permissions, and transfer of rights for published content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recommendations about author agreements, open-access licensing, and copyright notices in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: III.D Overlapping Publications — policies for duplicate, redundant, and salami publications; expectations for disclosure of related submissions/publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full guidance details acceptable overlap, required disclosures, and consequences for inappropriate duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: III.E Correspondence — standards for letters to the editor, responses, post-publication commentary, and handling of correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Recommendations include length, timeliness, and editorial handling practices in the full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: III.F Fees — policies regarding charges to authors or readers (e.g., page charges, processing fees), and disclosure of fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full guidance covers transparency, waiver policies, and ethical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplements, Theme Issues, and Special Series
rubrics_metrics.description: III.G Supplements, Theme Issues, and Special Series — standards for commissioning, sponsorship, peer review, and disclosure for special publication types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedures and transparency rules for supplements and sponsored content are in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorships and Partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: III.H Sponsorships and Partnerships — guidance on relationships with sponsors/partners and required disclosures to preserve integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examples and disclosure requirements in the full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: III.I Electronic Publishing — standards relevant to online publication, archiving, metadata, and digital practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Recommendations address online corrections, persistent identifiers, archiving, and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: III.J Advertising — policies on advertising content, separation from editorial content, and conflict-of-interest concerns related to ads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full document describes boundaries between advertising and editorial functions and disclosure expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals and the Media
rubrics_metrics.description: III.K Journals and the Media — guidance on press releases, media interactions, and responsible communication of research findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes best practices for accurate media representation and embargo policies in the full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: III.L Clinical Trials — policies related to clinical trial reporting, registration, and ethical reporting practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Recommendations include trial registration requirements, reporting standards, and links to registration resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a Manuscript for Submission to a Medical Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: IV.A Preparing a Manuscript for Submission to a Medical Journal — instructions on manuscript structure, required sections, formatting, and reporting standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed instructions (e.g., title page elements, abstracts, methods reporting, reporting guidelines like CONSORT) are in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending the Manuscript to the Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: IV.B Sending the Manuscript to the Journal — procedural guidance on submission process, cover letters, declarations, and required forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Recommendations list required statements, disclosure forms, and submission checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: V.A Use of AI by Authors — guidance and expectations for authors using artificial intelligence tools in the creation of manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full Recommendations provide rules on disclosure of AI use, attribution, and limitations on listing AI as an author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: V.B Use of AI by Reviewers — expectations and limitations for reviewers who use AI tools in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details (e.g., confidentiality, permitted uses, disclosure to editors) are in the full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' Role in Ensuring Responsible Use of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: V.C Editors' Role in Ensuring Responsible Use of AI — responsibilities for editors to set policy, enforce disclosure, and oversee AI-related practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Recommendations outline editorial policies, enforcement mechanisms, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Forms / Disclosure of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure Forms / Disclosure of Interest — site resources referenced for standard forms and mechanisms to report conflicts and interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site links to standardized disclosure forms and explains their use; see the downloadable forms and full Recommendations for detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials Registration (resource)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical Trials Registration — site resource and requirement references for registering clinical trials prior to enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Recommendation requires trial registration and links to registries; see full text for registry standards and timing requirements.
